hook: As the 40th US Secretary of Commerce, Gina Raimondo directed the CHIPS Act's semiconductor manufacturing buildout and issued the export control rules restricting advanced AI accelerators sold to China.
name: Gina Raimondo

quote.text: This rule will help safeguard the most advanced AI technology and ensure that it stays out of the hands of our adversaries.
quote.context: Gina Raimondo, Commerce Department AI diffusion rule announcement, January 13, 2025

reading.body:
US government control of semiconductor supply chains and AI model exports creates a direct constraint on compute availability, making policy choices about what chips leave the country as binding on AI scaling as physical power infrastructure.

Raimondo held the two levers that matter most for AI's upstream dependencies during the Biden administration. The CHIPS Act directs federal incentives to build domestic semiconductor manufacturing capacity, directly expanding the buildings and fabs where compute gets produced. The export controls restrict which accelerators and closed-weight models reach specific destinations, shrinking the compute available to adversaries regardless of their power or land. These are not separate policies. Together they form a strategy: build US capacity while blocking foreign access to the most advanced chips, which forces any nation outside allied networks to use older generations or build its own fabs.

The data shows what changed and when, but not the outcome. Export controls only constrain compute if they actually limit what reaches the target market, which depends on enforcement, circumvention, and whether stockpiles or design-arounds exist. CHIPS Act funding does not guarantee fabs actually open or run at full capacity. The policy layer sits upstream of the power and buildings layers, but only shapes behavior if implemented.

timeline.event: Sworn in as the 40th US Secretary of Commerce
timeline.impact: Takes charge of the department overseeing semiconductor policy, export controls and standards

timeline.event: Oversees Commerce Department implementation of the CHIPS and Science Act
timeline.impact: Directs the federal incentive program for domestic semiconductor manufacturing

timeline.event: Announces the Commerce Department's AI diffusion export control rule restricting advanced AI chips and closed-weight models
timeline.impact: Sets tiered export rules for advanced computing chips ahead of the administration transition

timeline.event: Leaves office as Secretary of Commerce at the end of the Biden administration
timeline.impact: Concludes her term as the 40th Secretary of Commerce

quick_facts: Served as the 40th US Secretary of Commerce from March 3, 2021 to January 20, 2025
Directed implementation of the CHIPS and Science Act's semiconductor manufacturing incentive program
Issued export control rules restricting sales of advanced AI accelerators to China, including a January 13, 2025 rule on AI model and chip diffusion
Left office at the end of the Biden administration on January 20, 2025
Joined the Council on Foreign Relations as a distinguished fellow in January 2025

achievements.title: US Secretary of Commerce, 2021 to 2025
achievements.impact: Directed the Commerce Department during passage and implementation of the CHIPS and Science Act, overseeing federal incentive awards for domestic semiconductor manufacturing.

achievements.title: Advanced AI chip export controls
achievements.impact: Issued Commerce Department rules restricting exports of advanced AI accelerators and, in January 2025, closed-weight AI models to strategic adversary destinations, while creating exceptions for allied nations.
